title: Diversity Patterns and Land Snail Assemblage Structure in the Forest‐Savannah Mosaic of Lamto Reserve, Central Côte d'Ivoire
content:
ABSTRACT

This study assessed the diversity and structure of land snail assemblages in the forest-savannah mosaic of the Lamto Reserve. Snails were sampled monthly for 1 year using direct search and litter sieving across eight plots (4 plots of 400 m2 per habitat type). A total of 749 individuals belonging to 18 species and 8 families were recorded. Abundance, species richness, Shannon diversity and evenness were higher in the forest island than in the annually burned savannah, whereas the Berger–Parker index was higher in the savannah, reflecting stronger dominance by few species. Community composition differed significantly between habitats. Two species were identified as indicators of the forest island, while none were associated with the annually burned savannah. Community structure was primarily associated with canopy cover, soil calcium, and pH. These findings highlight the combined role of vegetation structure, microclimatic conditions and soil properties in shaping terrestrial gastropod assemblages and identify forest islands as important biodiversity refugia for land snails within fire-maintained savannah landscapes.
